newsitem.title: USA: Democrats vie for retiring Florida lawmaker's seat.
newsitem.headline: Democrats vie for retiring Florida lawmaker's seat.

text.p: A former Tampa mayor and the majority leader of the state House face off Tuesday in a runoff election to chose the Democrat who will run for the seat being vacated by retiring 17-term Democratic Congressman Sam Gibbons.
The 11th district seat is seen as the one most vulnerable to Republican takeover of the three open House seats in Florida.
Former Mayor Sandy Freedman, 52, will compete against state House Majority Leader Jim Davis, 38, with the winner to vie for Gibbons' seat against Republican Mark Sharpe.

Political observers say the black vote will be key in a run-off race which traditionally brings out even fewer voters than a primary. In September, Freedman turned out more blacks than her three opponents combined as she won the primary with 35 percent of the vote. Davis finished second with 25 percent.

Sharpe, 36, ran against Gibbons twice and nearly upset him in 1994. He is a private school teacher, renominated without opposition. His previous campaigns, based on balancing the federal budget, have made him familiar to voters.

Supporters said Freedman has always been available to the black community in Tampa. Her decision to make Martin Luther King's birthday a local holiday before it was embraced by the U.S. government was well received by minorities.

Davis may have won some support from Freedman with his contention that she required Tampa police officers to store shotguns in cruiser trunks rather than in the front of the cars. Two police officers were seriously wounded last year and Davis has taken the position that had their shotguns been close at hand, they could have protected themselves.
